title: GW150914 reproducibility audit: public reanalysis succeeds partly while exact workflow reproduction remains bounded
summary: Meta-research/reanalysis record for GW150914. It distinguishes replication/confirmation/reanalysis from exact reproduction of the original workflow, and uses public-data cataloging as a denominator surface for external scrutiny.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0022 to pair the surviving-anomaly control with a workflow-transparency audit surface.

place.scope: Open gravitational-wave data and workflow-reproduction context

subjects.name: Original GW150914 analysis vs public-data/public-code reanalysis

claims.claim: Brown et al. describe an attempt to reproduce the GW150914 discovery-paper result using publicly available code on the Open Science Grid; they report reproducing the main result but not exactly reproducing the original LIGO analysis because the original dataset was not public.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass extraction changes the exact reproduction/available-dataset interpretation.

claims.claim: The 1-OGC open catalog paper reports using public Advanced LIGO O1 data to search for compact-object binary mergers; its three most significant signals correspond to GW150914, GW151226, and LVT151012, and it makes a complete catalog including sub-threshold candidates available.
what_would_change_status: A corrected 1-OGC source changes the public-data/candidate-catalog summary.

claims.claim: For the cube, GW150914 demonstrates an important distinction: confirmation, independent reanalysis, open event data, and exact original workflow reproduction are related but non-identical evidentiary achievements.
what_would_change_status: Future source review shows the distinction is already captured by another ledger and this record should be merged or split.

evidence_refs.support_type: metaresearch distinction encoded in this record

limitations: Does not reproduce code or compare workflow outputs.
Does not adjudicate all technical critiques or alternative analyses.

type_payload.denominator_surface: public event data, public code/workflow attempts, public O1 gravitational-wave data, external open catalog
type_payload.numerator_surface: original GW150914 discovery-paper result and collaboration analysis outputs
limits: Not a challenge to GW150914 detection status.
Not proof that all LIGO/Virgo analyses are exactly reproducible from public materials.
Uses abstract/page sources only in this pass; full methods review deferred.

handling_notes: Frame reproducibility limits as infrastructure/workflow facts, not as insinuations of misconduct.

unknowns: No full paper extraction or code execution.
No analysis of exact original/private dataset differences beyond abstract-level statement.
next_actions: Second-pass Brown et al. methods extraction.

Compare with non-GW exact-reproduction workflow audits.
